subject: Operationalizing No-Learn & Derivative Ban — evidence & subprocessor mapping
messages:
From: Sana Patel <sana@medisync.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference.com>, procurement@medisync.com
Date: 2026-11-15T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: No-learn and derivative restrictions - initial ask

David / team,

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. To move our security review forward we need explicit confirmation and operational details for two items in the proposed DPA: a strict no-training/no-derivatives commitment, and an evidence path that shows customer interaction data won't be used for model improvement or transferred to third-party model training pipelines. Specifically we need:

- Written confirmation the tenant for Medisync will be configured to never feed customer inputs or outputs into model-improvement pipelines (no adaptive training).
- A list of all subprocessors that will see or process customer interaction data (including engineering/ops oncall vendors).
- Evidence we can validate: audit log samples, subprocessor attestations, and the preferred delivery mechanism for evidence (SFTP/secure Drive).
- Residency guarantee for production inference (US-only) or fallback routing plan.

Our procurement team also asked for: a signed DPA (DocuSign is fine) and your SOC 2 Type II report (or equivalent). Can you provide a timeline for an ops evidence pack (logs/attestations) and a point of contact for technical onboarding?

Appreciate any detail you can share today — our security review team has a compliance window next week.

Thanks,
Sana Patel
Head of Security & Privacy
Medisync

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sana Patel <sana@medisync.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: No-learn and derivative restrictions - initial ask

Sana,

Thanks for the clear list. Short answer: yes, we can commit to a no-training/no-derivatives configuration for a dedicated Medisync tenant and provide an operational evidence bundle. I'll outline the specifics below and loop in ops/security to scope the deliverables.

Quick clarifying Qs to make sure the evidence meets your audit requirements:
- Which endpoints are in-scope (API only vs. Console/Embeddings)?
- Expected TPS/peak volume so Laura can size the dedicated pool and confirm routing constraints.
- Do you need raw transcripts for review or redacted samples (we can provide both, but raw will be under strict controls)?

Laura/Priyom, can you propose a 10-business-day evidence pack we can produce after we lock the tenant configuration? I'll also prepare the DocuSign DPA and SOC2 pointer for Sana.

Regards,
David Kim
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sana Patel <sana@medisync.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: No-learn and derivative restrictions - initial ask

Hi Sana — looping in operational detail here and a proposed delivery plan.

Summary of proposed configuration for a Medisync production tenant:
- Dedicated tenant (logical isolation) with a tenant-level flag: "no_learning = true". This prevents any token/event being routed to training/feedback queues.
- Model variants: we'll pin to a non-adaptive runtime and disable telemetry aggregation for Medisync.
- KV/prefix caching: prefix-only caching enabled; no persistent prompt dumps.
- Audit logs: request/response traces (redactable), routing logs, and service-level routing decisions for 90 days (can provide sample anonymized extracts).
- Subprocessor access: only authorized infra & security on-call; engineering access requires elevated request process and local approval. Full subprocessor inventory will be attached.

Proposed evidence pack (target: 10 business days after signed DPA and tenant activation):
1) Configuration snapshot (tenant flag, runtime config, pinned model version).
2) Subprocessor inventory & signed attestations.
3) Sample audit logs (redacted & hashed IDs, and an unredacted sample under NDA if required).
4) Network routing proof showing US-only egress for the tenant.
5) Ops runbook for onshore export/forensics (we'll use the attached ops-runbook-template.pdf as a base).

Delivery modes: secure Drive folder + SFTP drop for bulk logs. If you prefer, we can deliver a one-time encrypted tarball via the SFTP credentials we will provision.

Next steps I propose:
- Sana: confirm endpoints in-scope (API / Console / Embeddings).
- David: finalize the DPA language and send DocuSign link.
- Priyom: confirm the KMS and logging export timeline.

Laura Bennett
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>

Date: 2026-11-16T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: No-learn and derivative restrictions - initial ask

Adding infrastructure/security details and a couple of risk notes.

KMS & residency:
- We can enforce US KMS (customer-managed or Redwood-managed with US-only HSM). For Medisync I recommend Redwood-managed US KMS to simplify onboarding; we will add a KMS residency attestation to the evidence pack.
- On egress: production inference for the tenant will be routed through our us-east region. Failover to other regions will be disabled for the tenant to meet US-only residency.

Logs & proof:
- Audit logs (immutable append-only) with chain-of-custody metadata — we can provide SHA256-signed log samples and a short verification script.
- Subprocessor inventory attached as CSV with first-degree access descriptors. We will redact emails in public copies.

Operational caveats:
- If you plan high-frequency streaming sessions, we need to discuss batching behavior vs. latency; the evidence pack will note any short-lived KV caching events (we do not persist prompts beyond the session).
- APAC-specific restrictions: if Medisync expects EU/APAC traffic, we need to capture that in the DPA; for now we're aligned to US-only.

I've attached the current subprocessor_inventory.csv. I'll coordinate the log export window once the DPA is countersigned.

— Priyom
Infrastructure Security Lead
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: No-learn and derivative restrictions - initial ask — next steps

Sana / team,

Thanks — great to have alignment. Confirming immediate next steps and owners so there's no confusion:

Action items
- David (Legal): finalize DocuSign DPA and route to Sana for signature (DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/XYZ123-DPA). Target: EOD 2026-11-18.
- Laura (Ops): provision dedicated tenant with no_learning flag and arrange SFTP export window; prepare ops-runbook-template.pdf based evidence pack. Target: evidence snapshot within 10 business days of DPA signature.
- Priyom (Infra): prepare KMS residency attestation, export SHA256-signed log sample and subprocessor_inventory.csv. Target: KMS attestation + sample logs available with the evidence pack.
- Medisync (Customer): provide PO template and confirm endpoints in-scope (API only or Console/Embeddings).

Deliverables we'll attach to the Drive folder:
- ops-runbook-template.pdf (redwood)
- subprocessor_inventory.csv (redwood)
- Medisync_Security_QA.pdf (customer)
- evidence_drive_readme.txt (index of files + verification steps)

We will not feed any Medisync customer data into training or model-improvement queues for the tenant. We will include explicit language in the DPA and provide the evidence pack described above. If you need an unredacted log sample for legal review, please confirm an NDA channel and we'll arrange controlled access.

If procurement confirms DocuSign and PO timeline we'll start tenant provisioning immediately.

Best,
David Kim
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference
